facts.claim: Geoscience Australia's 'Sunrise, sunset and twilight times' online tool computes sunrise, sunset and twilight times using the National Gazetteer of Australia.

The Geoscience Australia tool (https://geodesyapps.ga.gov.au/sunrise) lets a user search the gazetteer for a place name, or enter a location by latitude and longitude (including locations outside Australia), choose a time zone, pick an event (sunrise/sunset, civil, nautical or astronomical twilight, sun transit time) and get results for a single day or a whole year.

Geoscience Australia defines sunset as the instant in the evening, under ideal meteorological conditions with standard refraction of the Sun's rays, when the upper edge of the Sun's disk is coincident with an ideal horizon.

Geoscience Australia defines the end of evening civil twilight as the instant when the centre of the Sun is 6 degrees below an ideal horizon; at this time, without moonlight, artificial lighting or adverse atmospheric conditions, large objects may be seen but no detail is discernible.

Geoscience Australia defines the end of evening nautical twilight as the instant when the centre of the Sun is 12 degrees below an ideal horizon; at this time, without moonlight, artificial lighting or adverse atmospheric conditions, it is dark for normal practical purposes.

Geoscience Australia notes that an ideal horizon is approximated when the surrounding terrain is flat and at the same height above sea level (the published times assume an ideal horizon and ideal meteorological conditions).

insider_details.detail: Look up sunset for your exact venue and wedding date (single-day result) rather than relying on a general city figure, then work the photo window and dinner start back from it. For an overseas venue, enter its latitude and longitude and choose the right time zone or UTC offset.

Published sunset assumes a flat, ideal horizon. At a venue with hills, cliffs, trees or buildings to the west, the sun drops out of view earlier than the listed time, so do a site walk at the same hour or ask your photographer when the light goes at that spot.

Usable soft light carries on after sunset until the end of civil twilight, but by then detail is no longer visible without artificial light. Book golden-hour portraits to finish around sunset and plan lighting (festoons, candles, uplights) to be on before civil twilight ends.

If guests move between ceremony and reception spaces outdoors (gardens, paths, terraces, coastal roads), schedule that move well before nautical twilight ends, when it is dark for practical purposes, or light the route.
